acceptanceCriteria.statement: Phase 0 ground truth: a plain answer to 'what actually costs 3 s' on entering PRISM, and whether option D's 7.8125 pc slab can stay under 50 ms (plan §8).

verifyVia.input: In the browser, warp to XIGMAG-2AE101G (IOTA AQUILA-6, near the core) and to Sol; enter PRISM in design 1 with and without the profiler; record query bounds, loop and density-call counts, per-callback times, both nav instances; run the option-D slab benchmark at the inner galaxy and Sol in the same browser.
verifyVia.observable: A written report (docs/WORKSTREAMS/naming-prism-segments-2026-10-02/PHASE0.md) naming the dominant cost with numbers, explaining the browser-vs-headless gap (3 s vs 0.2 s), and stating the measured option-D slab time at both locations against 50 ms.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: MEASURED LIVE 2026-10-02 at 7554b70 (Chrome 154, lane-A server :5175), report PHASE0.md, Astra second opinion folded in (PHASE0 §10). What costs the 3 s: the per-cell galaxy-density call, 62% of CPU in _spiralPotentialOnly (GalacticMap.js:844, 7 calls x 6 arms per cell). XIGMAG is at R = 17.0 kpc (the sparse rim, not near the core as this AC says), so its query box is 76.8 pc wide because _localCubeSize is used as a half-width (NavComputer.js:1188 -> :3698/:3750 vs :1593): 728,424 cells per 100 pc step vs Sol's 64,792, 1.86-2.18 s per query, 3.5-4.2 s per background callback, 32 callbacks, 116.6 s to fill the column (63,924 rows). Browser vs headless: the headless probes never tested R = 17; on identical bounds node takes 1.28-1.33 s and Chrome 2.0 s (same stars, same density calls), so the gap is ~10x box size times an observed ~1.5-1.65x engine factor; the profiler added nothing measurable. The cockpit nav keeps loading its own column alongside the overlay. Option D slab (7.8125 x 7.8125 x 100 pc) in Chrome: warm query 26.5-30.8 ms (max 32.1) inner galaxy, 29.2-30.9 ms (max 33.0) Sol, 22.6-26.5 ms XIGMAG, 4.0-4.4 ms bulge - all under 50 ms; with a cold feature cache 66-71 ms inner and 55 ms Sol - over 50 ms. Naming (~2 us/star) and multiplicity (~18-21 ms per dense slab, inferred) come on top. Verdict: Decision 0 stands, conditional on the Phase 3 loader slicing inside a slab under one deadline shared by both nav instances. Not yet measured (Phase 3): leaving PRISM, the six sort modes, cancelling a slab, swapping a same-size slab. Status sha note: 7554b70 is the code that was measured; the report lands in the commit after it, which cannot cite its own sha (no amend).

verifyVia.observable: Every case resolves to exactly one address and one identity; Sol resolves to sector N10 and the galactic centre to J10; sabotaging the half-open rule (closed upper edge) turns the face/corner tests red.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: HEADLESS, built 5b9ba76 + Astra fixup 12e1f05 (2026-10-02). src/generation/GalaxyGrid.js holds the frozen grid (2 kpc sectors, 16x16 regions, 16x16 prisms of 7.8125 pc, offset 1.00390625 kpc, 100 pc slabs, row 1 at the top) and one half-open addressOf/boundsOf for every level; HashGridStarfield stamps every star with ident = its generating (tier, cell), carried from the loop that made it, and key 'p:<tier>:<cx>:<cy>:<cz>'. Tests: GalaxyGrid.test.js (21) - faces, edges, corners, negatives, y = 0 is N1, round trip, injectivity over a sampled volume, Sol = N10, the centre = J10, and 'numbers every cell that can place a star in the box - and ONLY those' + 'a cell whose lowest star sits exactly on the excluded upper face is not a candidate' (Astra finding 4: slotOf now uses the generator's own placement arithmetic, 12 slots in Sol's N1 prism at 0.05 kpc, not 16); HashGridStarfield.identity.test.js (14) - every query and the sky carry the generating slot, endpoint stars included, and a 7-case fixture proves generation output byte-unchanged. Sabotage-checked: a closed upper edge turns the face/corner tests red; putting a tolerance back on the slot's upper face turns both slot tests red. Not in this AC (later phases): the live queries still accept both edges of their box, so one star can appear in two query results (same key, same owner) - the Phase 3 loader must filter by owner; and GalacticMap.hashCombine loses bits (a float multiply before |0), which is why same-seed stars exist - it stays unchanged here because fixing it would change which stars exist, and whether it is frozen with the names must be decided before Phase 4/5.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "The update build for the prism nav view needs to include performance optimization" — PRISM loads one 100 pc slab at a time with a deadline-based, resumable, cancellable loader that also budgets naming, merge, sort and publish. No main-thread task over 50 ms. Option D is confirmed here or reopened before any name is frozen.

verifyVia.input: Live, in both designs and both nav instances: enter PRISM, browse slabs, change every sort mode, jump with the segment bar, leave mid-load (cancel), re-enter cold — at XIGMAG-2AE101G (core) and at Sol; record a performance trace for each.
verifyVia.observable: No main-thread task longer than 50 ms in any trace (long-task list empty above 50 ms); keys pressed during loading act within one frame of being pressed (no queued burst).

acceptanceCriteria.maxRuling2026-10-02: "let's try to make the system work without this, but if needed we can come up with some kind of aesthetic-appropriate 'scanning' screen for loading windows" — target: NO loading screen (sliced loader keeps every task < 50 ms and the view live). Fallback only if that cannot be met: a 4th-gen-menu-style 'SCANNING' screen/overlay for the load window (see memory well-dipper-aesthetic-generations); it does not relax the 50 ms main-thread rule.
